item.title: Miscreants attempt to set fire to Humaiun Kobir's home in Sylhet
item.description:
A fire was set at the main gate of State Minister for Foreign Affairs-1 Humaiun Kobir's residence in the Dariapara area of Sylhet city early Friday.
The incident took place in the early hours of Friday, but no damage was reported.
Police said no petrol bomb was thrown at the gate. Instead, miscreants attempted to set it on fire by burning polythene.
A visit to the scene on Friday morning revealed burn marks on the iron grills of the main gate, with ashes from burnt polythene scattered on the ground.
Sylhet Metropolitan Police Deputy Commissioner (CTSB) Afzal Hossain, who is in charge of the media division, said someone had attempted to set fire to the main gate using polythene in the early hours.
Police went to the scene after receiving the information and found ashes beneath the gate, he added.
He said the minister's residence is located two houses beyond the main gate, inside the premises. A police outpost is also nearby.
The police have increased surveillance in the area, taking the incident seriously, he added.

item.title: Five suffer burn injuries in Mirpur warehouse fire
item.description:
Five people suffered burn injuries in a fire at a jhut (garment scraps) warehouse in the capital's Mirpur area on Thursday night.
The injured were identified as Moin, 15, Moyna, 36, Fatema, 9, Fatema, 30, and Nadira, 30. However, details about the injured were not available.
The fire broke out around 9pm at the warehouse in a house on Paridas Road of Mirpur-10, leaving five people injured.
The injured were rescued and taken to the emergency department of the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery around 12:30am on Friday.
Dr Sultan Mahmud Shikder, resident surgeon at the institute's emergency department, said all five patients sustained burns on their respiratory tract.

item.title: Bomb-like object left at Panchagarh DC office defused after 16hrs
item.description:
A bomb-like object found on the premises of the Panchagarh Deputy Commissioner's Office was defused nearly 16 hours later by the Special Response Battalion's (SRB) bomb disposal unit.
The object was detonated at a secure location around 11pm on Thursday.
An eight-point demand memorandum bearing the logo of the Awami League's district committee was later recovered from the debris.
According to administration sources, a man with his face covered left the red tape-wrapped object beside the office help desk early Thursday morning. Security was subsequently tightened, and the SRB bomb disposal unit was called in.
ASP Touhid of SRB-13 said the object was a locally made improvised explosive device (IED). A trained bomb disposal team recovered and safely detonated it.
Panchagarh Additional Deputy Commissioner Sohel Sultan Zulkarnain Kabir Steve said officials initially could not confirm whether the object was a bomb.
He added that the recovered memorandum would be sent to higher authorities, declining to disclose its contents, citing security concerns.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 13th among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 13th among the world's most polluted cities on Friday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 115 at 10:50a on Friday.
The city's air quality was classified as ‘moderate’, indicating little to no risk to the general public, although a small number of unusually sensitive people may experience minor health effects.
According to the AQI ranking, Pakistan's Lahore topped the list with a score of 465, followed by India's Delhi with 233 and Afghanistan's Kabul with 195.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around 7 million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Cummins' manager hits out at 'hysteria' around Sandpapergate
item.description:
Australia captain Pat Cummins' manager has hit out at the "hysteria" whipped up by the festering "Sandpapergate" scandal as Usman Khawaja said there was no reason for Cameron Bancroft to lie.
The Test skipper has come under huge pressure since Khawaja and then Bancroft claimed the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball in a Test at Cape Town in 2018.
Only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Bancroft -- who used the sandpaper -- were found to be responsible by a Cricket Australia probe.
Cummins strenuously denied he was aware of what was going on in a lengthy press conference a week ago, comments that have since come under scrutiny.
He has kept his head down since, and his manager Neil Maxwell described the criticism of him as "hysteria unfounded in reality".
"When you go through it all calmly and in detail, Pat's eight-year-long position and 68-minute Q&A (press conference) stands up," he said in a statement to Australian media.
"There is no serious case he was an architect of ball-tampering or knew sandpaper was going on the field.
"It's also true that the players who were suspended paid far too high a price," he added, referring to Smith, Warner and Bancroft.
"Year-long bans for ball-tampering that players in other countries did and were suspended for just a few games -- they have always been right to feel aggrieved by that."
The retired Khawaja reignited the controversy in his autobiography, alleging the whole team was in the know, and he was strongly backed by close friend Warner.
After Cummins' denials, Bancroft dropped a bomb in a newspaper column by also claiming "it was the whole team" while saying he felt "angry and betrayed" by the skipper.
Smith has so far stayed out of the furore.
The veteran batsman returned to training on Friday in Sydney for the first time since the scandal blew up again.
But he steered clear of reporters and made no comment.
Khawaja, who has pulled out of several media commitments since the story took off, told reporters who cornered him at an airport late Thursday that "there's no reason for Cameron to lie".
"I'm really happy that Cam felt safe enough to go out there and tell the story that he told about what happened," he said.
"I fully support Cameron and what he said. As a friend I will always have his back."
Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation and instead announced an independent forum would be launched for players to share their version of events.
Chief executive Todd Greenberg has backed Cummins and insisted the star bowler's version of events was not under scrutiny.

item.title: Vinicius ready for Real Madrid battle after Brazil revival
item.description:
Real Madrid have cut the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona down to three points, without the help of Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, who faces a fight to reclaim his place in the team.
Los Blancos have the chance to pull provisionally level with the Catalan giants on Saturday when they host Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu, with Vinicius in contention to play after serving a four-match domestic ban for hair-pulling.
In Vinicius's absence Jose Mourinho's side beat champions Barca in the Clasico at Camp Nou, as well as scoring wins over Sevilla, Racing Santander and Valencia.
The forward started in Madrid's Champions League victories over AEK Athens and RB Leipzig in that period but without finding the form which made him a vital player for Los Blancos over the past few years.
Vinicius, who joined Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018, carved out a reputation as one of the most dangerous attackers in world football, helping his side win the Champions League in 2022 and 2024.
However, this season he has struggled badly for form, with his only Madrid goal coming in August against Real Sociedad.
In the interim period Madrid's record signing Yan Diomande has adapted well to his new club and has four goals in his last eight appearances, staking his claim for the left wing spot.
During the international break Vinicius found some relief with Brazil, led by former Madrid coach Carlo Ancelotti.
The forward seemed unlocked, scoring five times in two friendlies against Japan and Singapore, which he hopes can be a platform to turn his domestic form around.
Vinicius admitted this summer, during which he was heavily linked with a departure from Madrid before ultimately penning a new deal until 2032, he let his standards slip.
Brazil suffered a surprise round-of-16 elimination at the World Cup by Erling Haaland's Norway, which took a toll.
"I don't think I prepared myself as well as I could have after the World Cup because the impact of that tournament is very significant for all Brazilians... being knocked out so early was something we didn't expect," he told reporters this week.
"I used the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years."
Vinicius said speculation on his future led to him feeling "overwhelmed" and he also highlighted the difficulty of staying at the peak of the game.
"I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to do it for so many years, reaching the same numbers," he added.
"I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve."
- Change of scene -
Vinicius's only other goal this season came in the previous international break, for Brazil against Australia in a friendly.
Former Real Madrid player Predrag Mijatovic told Spanish radio station Cadena Ser that Vinicius seems happier playing for Brazil than his club side.
"I think last summer hurt Vinicius quite a bit because he had that doubt about whether to stay or not, whether to renew his contract or not, and he has more competition this year, right?" said Mijatovic.
"Diomande is performing well in this position, and now Mourinho is the one who has to make his own decisions.
"What's clear is that Vini performs well when he's happy, and I see him much happier playing with his national team than playing here."
In previous campaigns the Brazilian has saved his best form for the second half of the season.
"Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals," said Vinicius.
In each of the past five seasons he has netted at least 22 times for Madrid.
On occasion Vinicius has faced criticism and whistles from the team's own fans, but Mourinho has shown patience, while urging the most lethal version of the forward to return.
"The Vini who is at his best kills games -- like he killed me in the past when I was with Benfica," said the veteran Portuguese coach in September.

item.title: Messi tops MLS salaries with Lewandowski next
item.description:
Lionel Messi remains the highest-paid player in Major League Soccer with $28.3 million in guaranteed compensation, according to a salary release Thursday by the players union, with Chicago's Robert Lewandowski second.
Argentine legend Messi topped the league list revealed by the MLS Players Association with compensation almost $8 million higher than last year, although his figures include only playing compensation and did not include income from other sources.
Messi signed a contract extension through 2028 last year.
Poland's Lewandowski, who joined the Chicago Fire earlier this year, was second overall with $19.51 million followed by Orlando's Antoine Griezmann of France at $13.938 million, South Korean star Son Heung-min of Los Angeles FC at $11.152 million and Swiss international Breel Embolo of Atlanta United at $10.81 million.
Among MLS clubs, Miami topped all teams in total guaranteed compensation at $59.37 million with Chicago second on $41.29 million, Atlanta third on $38.35 million, the Los Angeles Galaxy fourth on $34.91 million and LAFC fifth on $32.91 million.
The league's lowest total team compensation was Philadelphia Union at $12.64 million with Sporting Kansas City second lowest at $13.30 million and DC United third lowest at $14.55 million.
The figures are through October 9 and are annualized for players who arrived in the summer transfer period.

item.title: Govt installations on high alert amid nationwide unrest
item.description:
Government installations are increasingly coming under attack amid a rise in sabotage incidents allegedly linked to the activities-banned Awami League, prompting law enforcement agencies to step up surveillance and security across the country.
The incidents have intensified as December approaches, when ousted prime minister and Awami League President Sheikh Hasina has said she plans to return to Bangladesh from India.
Gopalganj has seen a particularly worrying rise in violence, while demonstrations, vandalism and arson have also been reported in at least 20 other districts.
In Dhaka, crude bomb explosions have occurred near lower courts, the Supreme Court premises, airport entrances, police station compounds and other important government installations.
According to Police Headquarters, 78 crude bomb explosions and 74 vehicle arson incidents were reported at 152 locations across the country between November 7 and 18. Police facilities and vehicles were also targeted during the period.
The 12-day tally includes arson and vandalism at three police installations, arson attacks on 18 police vehicles, cocktail explosions at two police facilities and damage to another police vehicle in an explosion.
A total of 38 cases have been filed in connection with the incidents, and 63 people have been arrested, Police Headquarters said in a statement on Thursday. However, it did not specify how many cases had been filed in relation to all the reported incidents.
Sabotage was also reported in Dhaka and 16 districts during the Awami League's lockdown programme on November 19. The districts were Gopalganj, Chattogram, Gazipur, Natore, Mymensingh, Tangail, Kishoreganj, Chandpur, Narayanganj, Netrokona, Rajshahi, Panchagarh, Rangpur, Pabna, Sunamganj and Sylhet.
Security analysts say the incidents have created fresh challenges for law enforcement, raising concerns over public safety. They stress the need not only to identify and arrest those involved but also to uncover the planning, organisers and sources of funding behind the attacks.
Kamarum Munira, assistant inspector general (media and public relations) at Police Headquarters, said police had increased intelligence gathering, surveillance and patrols, set up checkpoints and taken steps to ensure rapid responses to incidents.
She said police would remain on high alert to prevent the banned organisation and the party whose activities have been prohibited from carrying out sabotage. No one would be allowed to create anarchy or undermine law and order, and attempts at sabotage would be dealt with firmly, she added.
During the Awami League's lockdown and the Chhatra League's blockade programmes, several crude bomb explosions were reported near government facilities in Dhaka, alongside arson attacks on vehicles.
Explosions were reported inside the Pallabi police station compound and outside the police stations in Khilkhet, Jatrabari, Khilgaon and Adabor. Other reported targets included the Criminal Investigation Department headquarters in Malibagh, the police lines in Rajarbagh, Dhaka University, the Supreme Court, the lower court premises, the Bangladesh Television building and the entrances to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport. Explosions were also reported beneath the metro rail line in Agargaon and in Mirpur-11.
Deputy Commissioner Akhtar Hossain of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's media wing said the attackers had targeted government installations but had so far failed to cause major damage in the capital.
“Security has been strengthened across Dhaka in view of the current situation,” he said, adding that police were working both to protect government installations and ensure the safety of city residents.
Inspector General of Police Md Ali Hossain Fakir said on Thursday that police were performing their duties professionally in accordance with the country's laws and regulations.
He urged people not to be misled by conspiracies, rumours or propaganda.

item.title: Tarique Rahman marks first birthday as prime minister
item.description:
November 20 marks the 62nd birthday of Tarique Rahman, Bangladesh's prime minister and chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). It is his first birthday since assuming the country's highest executive office following the 13th parliamentary election in February 2026.
Born on November 20, 1965, Tarique Rahman grew up in a family deeply involved in Bangladesh's political history. His father, Ziaur Rahman, was a freedom fighter and former president, while his mother, Khaleda Zia, served three times as prime minister.
His political journey began in 1988, when he joined the BNP in Gabtali, Bogra. He became a member of the Bogra district BNP in 1993 and played an organizational role in his mother's election campaigns in 1991 and 2001. In 2002, he was appointed senior joint secretary-general of the party.
His political career faced a major setback in 2007, when the military-backed caretaker government arrested him. Following his release, he travelled to London for medical treatment, beginning nearly 17 years away from Bangladesh.
Despite living abroad, he remained involved in BNP activities and led the party as it faced arrests, legal cases and restrictions during the Awami League government's tenure. In 2018, he became the BNP's acting chairman while Khaleda Zia was imprisoned.
The July-August 2024 mass uprising, which resulted in around 1,400 deaths and brought an end to Sheikh Hasina's nearly 16-year rule on August 5, 2024, marked a turning point in the country's political landscape.
Tarique Rahman returned to Bangladesh on December 25, 2025. Five days later, his mother died. On January 9, 2026, he assumed the BNP chairmanship.
The BNP subsequently won 211 seats in the February 12, 2026 parliamentary election, paving the way for him to become prime minister. The European Union Election Observation Mission described the electoral process as credible and broadly in line with democratic standards.
His first birthday as prime minister comes with considerable expectations. Good governance, accountability, economic stability, employment, quality education, improved healthcare and stronger democratic institutions remain among the key challenges facing his government.
Since taking office, the government has introduced several initiatives, including the Family Card and Farmer Card, agricultural loan waivers for small and marginal farmers, and plans for a Health Card. Other measures include expanding higher education opportunities for girls, introducing mid-day meals in primary schools, clearing outstanding dues of retired MPO-listed teachers and providing honorariums to imams and muezzins.
The government has also pursued canal excavation, tree plantation, increased investment and job creation as part of its efforts to improve living standards and strengthen the economy.
Upon returning home, Tarique Rahman told supporters: "I have a plan." The statement has since become associated with his government's development agenda.
His leadership will ultimately be assessed against the delivery of these commitments, the protection of democratic institutions and the ability to address the country's economic and social challenges.
As he turns 62, the occasion marks both a personal milestone and a significant point in his political journey. The responsibilities of governing now place the focus on translating electoral promises into tangible improvements in people's lives.
Happy birthday to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

item.title: Security tightened at Dhaka airport amid sabotage fears
item.description:
Security has been tightened at the third terminal and hangar gate of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport following intelligence reports of possible sabotage targeting the two key facilities.
The third terminal, scheduled to be inaugurated on December 16, has remained a major focus of public attention. The hangar area is also considered critical as it houses aircraft operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines and other carriers.
Authorities have stepped up security at both locations, deploying uniformed and plainclothes personnel for round-the-clock surveillance. Monitoring of civilian staff working in the areas has also been increased.
Air Commodore Asif Iqbal, member (security) of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), said security measures were already in place at airports but had been strengthened in the current situation.
“Instructions have been issued to all airports to maintain round-the-clock security,” he said.
Intelligence sources said a group had been carrying out sabotage activities at different locations across the country. Several crude bomb explosions have reportedly occurred near police stations and important installations in the capital, including entrances to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
The sources also referred to the recent recovery of two high-powered grenades near Rajshahi Airport, saying intelligence agencies had received information about a possible attack there.
The third terminal is one of the airport's most prominent infrastructure projects and is awaiting inauguration after years of construction. Its opening has attracted considerable attention at home and abroad.
Intelligence officials believe an attack ahead of the inauguration could draw widespread media coverage, raise questions about the country's security arrangements and potentially delay the opening.
Following the intelligence alerts, the relevant authorities were informed and additional security measures were introduced around the two facilities.
The third terminal is under continuous surveillance, with security personnel monitoring the area and CCTV and AI-enabled camera systems being used to strengthen oversight.
Security has also been reinforced around the hangar gate, with surveillance extended to the surrounding area. People entering the restricted facilities, including personnel reporting for duty, are being subjected to additional checks and monitoring.
Authorities have not disclosed further details of the alleged threat or any specific suspects.

item.title: India declines comment on Bangladesh’s internal affairs
item.description:
India has declined to comment on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s allegation that protests by the activities-banned Awami League were being orchestrated at the direction of its “masters across the border”, while reiterating its commitment to constructive relations with Bangladesh.
Asked about the prime minister’s remarks, Indian External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Friday: “I have no comments on the internal developments in Bangladesh.”
At a rally in Lalmonirhat on Thursday, Tarique accused Awami League leaders of working against Bangladesh’s interests and conspiring against the country to please those who had sheltered them across the border, without naming India.
The remarks came amid violence in several parts of Bangladesh during a nationwide lockdown called by the Awami League on Thursday. The party had urged supporters to disrupt businesses and public transport as part of a weeklong protest campaign.
Reiterating New Delhi’s longstanding position, Jaiswal said India wanted positive, constructive and forward-looking relations with Bangladesh, rooted in shared history and cultural ties between the two peoples.
On the extradition request for ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in India since August 2024, Jaiswal said he had no fresh information. He had previously said the request was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.
Hasina’s London-based lawyers sent a second request to the Bangladesh High Commission on Thursday seeking a passport and national identity card for her. Dhaka has rejected an earlier application and renewed its request for her return.
Asked about the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, which is due to expire on December 12, Jaiswal said the India-Bangladesh Joint Rivers Commission was the established mechanism for discussing water-sharing and transboundary river issues.
He reiterated that India remained committed to constructive ties with Bangladesh while safeguarding its own interests.

item.title: IGP, SRB and BGB chiefs visit Gopalganj amid security concerns
item.description:
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir, along with the chiefs of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), visited Gopalganj on Friday to assess the district’s security situation.
They arrived in the district on Friday morning. The delegation also included SRB Director General Faruk Ahmed and BGB Director General Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui.
Police Headquarters sources said the officials would review the overall law and order situation and attend a special welfare meeting organised by the district police.
The visit comes after a series of violent incidents in Gopalganj on November 15, allegedly involving activists of the activities-banned Awami League.
The incidents included attacks on police vehicles, arson and vandalism at the home of Tungipara municipal BNP President Imdad Molla, and attacks on several BNP offices and properties linked to party leaders.
A BNP office at Patgati Bazar was also attacked and set on fire. Later, the Tungipara Upazila BNP and Jubo Dal offices were torched.
The house of former upazila Swechchhasebak Dal president Jasim Sheikh and a shop owned by Mahmud Member in the Chowrangi area were also set ablaze, while the chamber of municipal BNP General Secretary Dr Zafar was vandalised.

item.title: Bangladesh climbs to 97th in UN e-government index
item.description:
Bangladesh has moved up three places to rank 97th among 194 countries in the United Nations E-Government Development Index (EGDI) 2026, entering the top 100 for the first time.
The country was ranked 100th in the 2024 edition. Its score rose to 0.6893 in 2026, the highest in its history, keeping Bangladesh in the “High EGDI” category.
Bangladesh also achieved record scores in two components of the index. Its Online Service Index (OSI) score stood at 0.81, while its Telecommunication Infrastructure Index (TII) score reached 0.69, according to the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology.
The findings were published in the 2026 UN E-Government Survey, a biennial report prepared by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs. The Republic of Korea topped the global ranking.
The EGDI measures countries’ readiness, capacity and progress in using digital technologies to deliver public services. It combines scores across three areas: online services, telecommunications infrastructure and human capital.
The global average score increased by 4.6% to 0.6675 in 2026, from 0.6382 in 2024. Bangladesh’s score is above the latest global average.
Of the 194 countries assessed, 151 are now classified in the “High” or “Very High” EGDI groups, up from 138 in 2024.

item.title: Rashed alleges Hasina’s forged signature in passport, NID application
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan has alleged that a forged signature of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina was used in an authorisation letter submitted to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi as part of an application seeking a new passport and national identity card for her.
The letter was submitted by London-based law firm Matrix Chambers, which sought to represent Hasina in the matter through a power of attorney bearing her purported signature.
In a Facebook post on Thursday night, Rashed said he had spoken to an official at the High Commission, who reportedly found evidence of forgery after verification.
He questioned the use of an English signature, claiming Hasina had signed official documents in Bengali during her tenure and that her signature should match the one recognised in her NID records.
Meanwhile, Matrix Chambers barrister Steven Powles sent another letter to the acting high commissioner on Thursday, seeking an update on the passport and NID application. The latest letter reportedly included a certification from Hasina.
Rashed also criticised the law firm, alleging that it had failed to verify the form of signature used by Hasina before submitting the authorisation letter.

item.title: Khalilur calls for swift implementation of ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide
item.description:
United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) President and Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman has called for the swift implementation of the International Court of Justice's (ICJ) landmark ruling recognising Myanmar's atrocities against the Rohingya as genocide.
He outlined four priorities: ensuring justice and accountability for those responsible, facilitating safe and dignified repatriation, providing compensation and humanitarian assistance, and preventing a recurrence of such atrocities.
He made the calls while addressing a rally at a Rohingya refugee camp in Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar, around 8:30am on Friday.
Rohingya representatives, Bangladeshi and UN officials, and journalists attended the event.
Khalilur Rahman began his speech by paying tribute to the Rohingya killed during Myanmar's 2017 military crackdown.
"Yesterday (Thursday), the world's highest court spoke in The Hague. The court spoke the name of the Rohingya. Its decision is clear: what happened to them in 2017 was genocide. For the first time in history, the International Court of Justice has found a state responsible for committing genocide," he said.
He said the court found that Myanmar's security forces had carried out mass killings, sexual violence and abuses against women and children in northern Rakhine with the intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population.
At least 10,000 people were killed, and entire villages were wiped out, he said, adding that the court had found the crimes were committed with the intent to destroy the Rohingya community. The court also recognised the Rohingya as a distinct ethnic group in Myanmar.
No court ruling could bring back the dead or heal all wounds, Khalilur Rahman said, but justice begins with establishing the truth. The ruling has given international recognition to the Rohingya's long-standing persecution and deprivation, he added.
Describing the ICJ ruling as final and binding, with no scope for appeal, the UNGA president said it must be translated into action rather than remain on paper.
First, those suspected of involvement in the crimes must face investigation, prosecution and punishment under the Genocide Convention. Myanmar must take effective steps and introduce necessary reforms to its national laws and judicial system.
Second, safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation must be ensured by guaranteeing the Rohingya's citizenship rights, freedom of movement and protection from discrimination and persecution.
No Rohingya should be returned to an unsafe environment, and their views and aspirations must be prioritised in the repatriation process, he said.
Third, affected Rohingya must receive adequate compensation. Individuals and communities should be compensated for losses that cannot be remedied through the restoration of property.
Humanitarian assistance in the refugee camps must also continue until safe repatriation becomes possible. This responsibility cannot be left to Bangladesh alone, and the international community and development partners must increase their support and funding.
Fourth, Myanmar must introduce effective legal and institutional reforms to prevent similar atrocities in the future. These should include better training for security forces, civilian oversight and measures to protect the Rohingya.
Responding to questions from journalists, Khalilur Rahman said the UN General Assembly could take decisions on the matter if the ICJ ruling was not implemented.
He described the ruling as a landmark decision, saying no similar verdict had been delivered before.
Failure to comply would call into question the entire international system built through the international community and various organisations, he said.
"To maintain public confidence in international law and multilateral cooperation, we must ensure that the ruling is implemented," he said.
Referring to Article 94 of the UN Charter, he said UN member states are obligated to comply with ICJ rulings. If a state fails to implement a ruling, the matter can be taken to the UN Security Council.
He also pledged to continue discussions with member states on the issue in his capacity as president of the General Assembly.
Khalilur Rahman thanked Gambia, the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the 11 states that intervened in the case, the UN investigative team, and the government and people of Bangladesh for their roles in the legal battle.
He also praised the hospitality of local communities in Ukhiya and Teknaf for sheltering the Rohingya and highlighted the courage of survivors and women who testified before the court.
Addressing the Rohingya, he said he had come to the refugee camps to stand beside them, not from New York.
He pledged to convey their voices to all 193 UN member states, particularly those of women, children and young people.
"I want November 19, 2026, to be remembered in history as the day the journey towards the Rohingya's return home began. Justice has been established in The Hague. Now it is our responsibility to implement that justice here in these camps and in your respective villages in Rakhine," he said.
UN Interim Resident Coordinator Carol Flore-Smereczniak and Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner (RRRC) Mizanur Rahman, among other officials, attended the rally.

item.title: Kobir: Fugitives can’t be brought back from Delhi through violence
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Friday said attempts to pave the way for the return of fugitive individuals from Delhi on commercial flights by resorting to violence would not work, noting that the process of bringing them back to Bangladesh would be pursued under the extradition treaty.
“Here, no fugitive terrorist can be brought back to Bangladesh from Delhi even by throwing petrol bombs; I mean, as a commercial passenger. That will actually happen through the extradition treaty,” he said while talking to reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Kobir described the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, as a “terrorist organisation”, saying the government would take strong action against those involved in petrol bomb attacks, arson and other acts of violence.
He dismissed concerns that such incidents could tarnish Bangladesh's image internationally, saying the government was determined to deal with the perpetrators through law enforcement agencies and the judicial process.
“No, I mean, look – 'Joy Bangla' has now been transformed into a fleeing slogan,” the state minister said in response to a question from a journalist about whether the incidents of arson were damaging Bangladesh's image abroad.
He alleged that the Awami League had turned into a terrorist party and said its activities had been suspended over what he described as terror-related activities.
“Now, basically, Awami League is suspended for terrorist activities. It is now almost on the line of being regulated as a terrorist party,” Kobir said.
He alleged that the party's leaders, including those staying abroad, were inciting acts of violence and said law enforcement agencies were working to bring those responsible to justice.
“The law enforcement agencies are working on it, and with the long arm of justice we will grab them. So, there is no place for terrorists - terrorists of Bangladesh - and there is no place for terrorists anywhere in the world,” the state minister said.
Describing the recent incidents as sporadic acts of terrorism, he said those involved in petrol bomb attacks and arson would not be able to intimidate the people.
“It has now virtually reduced itself to a sporadic terrorist organisation. Here a petrol bomb, there they will light a fire and run away,” Kobir said.
He added that the government would not allow such activities to undermine public confidence or disrupt the country's progress. “The people of the country will never be terrified by these small terrorist cowards,” he said.
The state minister said Bangladesh was moving towards a new phase of development, with opportunities for all, and was also making progress in its international engagement and visibility.
“The Bangladesh government is there, and the government has ensured that this Bangladesh moves to be a new Bangladesh where there are opportunities for all. And we will take this country forward,” he said.
Kobir expressed confidence that Bangladesh's international profile would continue to rise, saying the country was becoming one that its citizens could take pride in.
“Now Bangladesh is moving forward nationally as well as internationally. And its visibility, which I shared with you, is now going to another level,” he said, also acknowledging the role of the media community in this progress.

item.title: Bad weather strands 1,000 tourists on St Martin’s Island
item.description:
Nearly 1,000 tourists, including 96 teachers and students from two universities, have been stranded on Saint Martin’s Island as vessel services remain suspended due to adverse weather.
With their stay on the island extended, many are running out of money to cover food expenses, leaving them in financial difficulty. Concern has also mounted after a student from one of the university groups was injured in a motorcycle accident.
The 96 stranded university members include 31 from the Department of Social Work at Jamalpur University of Science and Technology (JUST) and 65 from the Department of Bangla at Rajshahi University (RU).
A JUST student was injured in a motorcycle accident, dislocating his kneecap (patella). As the island lacks adequate medical facilities, arrangements are being made to take him to Teknaf for advanced treatment.
The JUST group consists of two teachers and 29 students. Students from the department's 2021-22 academic session went to Saint Martin’s Island on November 17 for a batch tour and were scheduled to return on Thursday.
However, they became stranded after vessel services were suspended due to adverse weather.
Hossain Mahmud, a lecturer in the department, told reporters that they were informed late on Wednesday that vessel services would be suspended on Thursday. They were later told that services would also remain suspended on Friday, leaving them in a difficult situation. Their food budget has nearly run out after the prolonged stay on the island, he added.
JUST Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Amir Hossain said 31 members of the university, including two teachers, were stranded on the island and one student had been injured. He said the group was also facing financial difficulties and that the university was contacting the relevant authorities to bring them back as soon as possible.
Shahidul Islam, an assistant community medical officer at Saint Martin’s Hospital, said the injured student had received first aid. However, the island lacks adequate facilities to provide the necessary treatment.
The Coast Guard said arrangements had been made to take the student to Teknaf for further treatment, but transferring him remained risky due to unfavourable weather.
Saint Martin’s Union Parishad Chairman Foyezul Islam said the local council would provide assistance if the stranded teachers and students faced financial difficulties. He added that the council was keeping in touch with them and monitoring their situation.

item.title: Kobir: Bangladesh to push for Rohingya return to Myanmar within 1-1.5 years
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Friday said Bangladesh would expedite talks with the United Nations and bilateral partners to secure safe passage for Rohingyas back to Myanmar within a year to a year and a half.
He said Bangladesh would work with UN agencies, key regional partners and other stakeholders to establish conditions for safe return and described prompt and sustainable repatriation as the only effective solution to the protracted crisis.
“We will pursue these discussions vigorously so that we can provide safe passage within a year to a year and a half,” he told reporters at a media briefing on the International Court of Justice (ICJ) judgement.
Bangladesh on Thursday called upon the government of Myanmar to carry out its obligations under the historic judgement, delivered by the ICJ, ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during a brutal military crackdown in 2017, "promptly, fully and effectively."
Bangladesh, in a statement, also urged the international community to ensure full, effective and expeditious implementation of this historic verdict.
In particular, Bangladesh reiterated that repatriation of the Rohingyas to their homeland in Myanmar remained the only viable solution to the crisis.
"Bangladesh believes that the judgement will serve as a critical catalyst for safe, voluntary and dignified return of the Rohingyas to Myanmar," said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in its press statement.
Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury and Additional Foreign Secretary (Public Diplomacy and Other Priority Matters) AKM Shahidul Karim were also present at the media briefing.
Kobir said the ruling gave Bangladesh a stronger legal basis to press for safe repatriation and compensation for affected communities.
He outlined the timeframe in response to a question on how Bangladesh would accelerate repatriation, saying any return would depend on putting safeguards in place in Myanmar’s Rakhine State so that the Rohingyas could go home safely and rebuild their lives.
The state minister said Bangladesh would also work through the UN system and with its bilateral partners to ensure that compensation reached Rohingya communities affected by the genocide.
Asked whether Dhaka would pursue a bilateral mechanism with Myanmar to determine compensation, he said bilateral efforts alone could not secure the necessary reparations and that the process would require the involvement of several countries and agencies.
Kobir said financial compensation could never make up for the lives lost or the suffering of bereaved families.
Bangladesh would, however, he said, seek to persuade Myanmar to provide compensation and take other measures that would help surviving family members return and rebuild their lives.
The state minister said Bangladesh would work within the UN system to press for follow-up on compensation if The Gambia, a party to the case, brought the matter before the UN Security Council.
Asked whether Bangladesh would formally propose deploying an international peacekeeping force in Rakhine, he said Dhaka would engage a wider range of UN agencies and bilateral partners if the matter came before the council. He gave no commitment to a formal peacekeeping proposal.
Kobir said the ICJ had found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingyas in Rakhine State.
He described it as the first judgement in the court’s history to find a state responsible for committing genocide.
The state minister said the court recognised the Rohingyas as a distinct ethnic group with their own language, culture and identity, and noted that discriminatory laws, restrictions and campaigns of hatred had progressively curtailed their rights over several decades.
He said the court found that Myanmar had failed to prevent genocidal acts by civilians acting alongside its security forces and to preserve evidence as required by its 2020 order on provisional measures.
Kobir said the court directed Myanmar to enact effective legislation to prevent genocide, end ongoing violence and investigate individuals reasonably suspected of involvement in genocide, with prosecution and punishment where appropriate.
The ruling also addressed reparations for victims through restitution and compensation, he added.
The state minister said the judgement was final, could not be appealed and was legally binding on the parties to the case.
Bangladesh, which hosts over 1.3 million forcibly displaced Rohingyas, had closely followed the proceedings although it was not a party to the case, he said.
Kobir thanked the government and people of The Gambia for bringing the case on November 11, 2019, as well as the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the 11 countries that filed written declarations before the court.
He also acknowledged the Rohingya community’s years of advocacy and the support of host communities in Cox’s Bazar.
The state minister urged the international community to act swiftly on the judgment and called on development partners and donors to continue humanitarian assistance for displaced Rohingyas and Bangladeshi host communities until repatriation is complete.

item.title: Cheaper winter vegetables fail to ease pressure on consumers
item.description:
Prices of some winter vegetables have started to fall, but consumers in Dhaka are still struggling with high prices of green chillies, eggs, fish and meat, leaving little room for relief in household budgets.
"Even when the price of one item falls, another goes up. Household expenses are not limited to vegetables; we also need rice, oil, fish and meat. But with no increase in income, the same budget cannot even cover half of what it used to. We have to calculate every expense and cut back on many things just to manage our shopping," said Rafik Nabi, who was shopping at Rai Saheb Bazar in Old Dhaka on Friday morning.
Vegetable trader Nayeem Hasan said prices of some items had fallen as supplies of winter vegetables increased, although green chilli prices remained high.
"We collect vegetables from the wholesale market in Shyambazar and have to set our selling prices based on what we pay there," he said.
A visit to Rai Saheb Bazar on Friday found that increased supplies of winter vegetables had brought down the prices of some items, while many others remained expensive.
Old potatoes were selling for Tk25-30 per kg, papaya for Tk30, pointed gourd and okra for Tk50 each, and snake gourd for Tk60.
Eggplants were priced at Tk60-100 per kg, beans at Tk60-80, bitter gourd, yardlong beans and ridge gourd at Tk80 each.
Radishes were selling for Tk40-50 per kg, cauliflower for Tk30-40 each and bottle gourds for Tk50-70 apiece. New potatoes remained expensive at Tk120-150 per kg.
Among leafy vegetables, red amaranth was selling for Tk15 per bunch, spinach for Tk20 and Malabar spinach for Tk30.
Fish prices also remained high. Tilapia was selling for Tk180-200 per kg, pangas for Tk180, rohu for Tk280-350 and catla for Tk300-500. Depending on size and quality, ilish was priced at Tk800-2,000 per kg.
A dozen farm-produced brown eggs were selling for Tk140, while white eggs cost Tk130.
In the meat market, broiler chicken was selling for Tk190 per kg, Sonali chicken for Tk320, beef for Tk800 and mutton for Tk1,200 per kg.
