item.description:
Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan has alleged that a forged signature of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was used in an authorisation letter submitted to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi in connection with her efforts to get a new passport and national identity card.
London-based law firm Matrix Chambers approached the High Commission with a power of attorney bearing Hasina’s purported signature, seeking to represent her in the matter.
The signature came under scrutiny as Sheikh Hasina is generally known to sign official documents in Bengali rather than English.
In a Facebook post on Thursday night, Rashed alleged that the signature on the authorisation letter had been forged.
“I have spoken in detail with an official working at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi about this matter. After verification, they found evidence of signature forgery in the letter,” he wrote.
Rashed said Hasina had used a Bengali signature on all documents during her tenure as Prime Minister.
“Hasina is one person, and she should have only one signature. Even in applications of this kind, a signature other than the one previously used or recognised in the NID cannot be used. Nor is there any scope for using a forged signature,” he said.
Meanwhile, Barrister Steven Powles of Matrix Chambers sent another letter to the acting High Commissioner of Bangladesh in New Delhi on Thursday, seeking an update on his earlier letter seeking a passport and NID card for Hasina.
A certification from Hasina was also attached to the latest letter, according to the information available.
Rashed further alleged that Matrix Chambers had made a mistake while attempting to forge Hasina’s signature.
“Thieves always leave some trace behind. Matrix Chambers, the London-based law firm, made the same mistake while sending the letter with a forged signature of Sheikh Hasina. They could at least have asked her once whether she signs in Bengali or English,” he wrote.
Rashed also questioned whether Hasina did not understand English well or whether the lawyers at Matrix Chambers were unfamiliar with Bengali.

item.title: BGB foils BSF attempt to push in 4 through Meherpur border
item.description:
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) foiled an attempt by the Border Security Force (BSF) of India to push four unidentified men into Bangladesh through the border in Gangni upazila of Meherpur district early Friday.
According to a BGB, the incident took place around 2am in the area under the jurisdiction of Rangmahal Border Outpost (BOP) of Kushtia Battalion (47 BGB).
The attempt was detected and thwarted due to intelligence information, the alert presence of BGB patrol teams along the border and their prompt action.
Later, following the firm stance and effective initiatives of the Kushtia Battalion commander, BSF's Dighalkandi camp under its 11th Battalion took the four men back inside India's barbed-wire fence around 7:45am.
Kushtia Battalion Commander Lt Col Rashed Kamal Rony said regular patrols had been strengthened in the border area.
He said BGB personnel were maintaining the highest level of vigilance and professionalism to ensure overall border security.

item.title: National Bank software faces shutdown risk over unpaid fees
item.description:
National Bank PLC is facing an international arbitration case over unpaid software maintenance and licensing fees, raising concerns about the continuity of its core banking operations and the security of depositors' money.
Singapore-based FDS Global Pte Ltd, supplier of the bank's Temenos core banking software, and its Bangladeshi partner BG Interactive Limited have jointly filed arbitration proceedings against National Bank PLC and Switzerland-based Temenos Headquarters SA at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC).
According to arbitration documents, the notices were filed on October 30 over alleged breaches of a December 2019 agreement. The cases were registered under reference numbers ARB 516/26/MNH and ARB 517/26/MNH.
On November 5, the SIAC secretariat asked the respondents to submit written responses within 14 days.
Banking sources said National Bank had failed to pay annual maintenance contract (AMC) charges and other related fees since 2024, despite repeated reminders from the software providers. They alleged that the bank's board and senior management had failed to resolve the issue.
Core banking software supports almost all essential banking services, including account management, branch transactions, automated teller machine (ATM) operations, card services, online banking and interbank fund transfers.
Any disruption to the system could seriously affect banking services, particularly as National Bank is already struggling with a prolonged liquidity crisis. More than 2 million depositors could face uncertainty if the dispute remains unresolved.
However, the filing of arbitration proceedings does not automatically mean that software services will be suspended.
Meanwhile, despite changes to its board following recent political developments, National Bank has yet to achieve a sustainable recovery.
Earlier, Bangladesh Bank arranged Tk700 crore in liquidity support through state-owned Sonali Bank following a High Court ruling concerning depositors' demands for the return of their money.
The latest dispute has raised further questions about the bank's financial management and its ability to meet essential operational expenses despite central bank support.
Banking observers said an urgent resolution was necessary to ensure uninterrupted services and restore depositor confidence.

item.title: Mintoo urges people to cooperate with law enforcement agencies
item.description:
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo on Friday urged people not to take the law into their own hands but to cooperate with the law enforcement agencies.
"We have been victims of oppression and persecution for the past 17 years. The people have supported us and brought us to power. The nation is currently at peace, and we wish to maintain that peace," he said while speaking as the chief guest at a meeting held at Daganbhuiyan Upazila Parishad auditorium in Feni.
Mintoo said those, who are legally banned, are trying to create anarchy in the country but they will not be allowed to do so in any way.
The minister said those involved in past acts of oppression and current illegal activities must be brought to justice, cautioning that no innocent person should be harassed out of personal vendetta.
Calling upon all abide by laws, Mintoo asked BNP leaders and activists to inform law enforcement immediately upon learning of any plans for sabotage.
"Do not take the law into your own hands. If you do, how would we be any different from 'them'?" he said.

item.title: 80 pirates arrested, 115 firearms seized in Sundarbans in over 22 months
item.description:
Bangladesh Coast Guard has arrested 80 pirates and seized 115 firearms and 518 rounds of ammunition in the Sundarbans over the past 22 and a half months.
Between January 1 and November 19, the Coast Guard West Zone also rescued 135 people, including 132 fishermen held hostage by pirates, two tourists, and a resort owner.
During the same period, 64 members of several pirate gangs surrendered to the force with 48 locally made and foreign firearms, 617 rounds of live ammunition, 25 rounds of pistol ammunition and 413 rounds of airgun pellets, among other weapons and equipment.
Coast Guard media officer Lt Commander Suman Al Mukit confirmed the information, saying 63 of the operations resulted in significant arms and ammunition seizures, arrests of bandits and the rescue of abducted people.
He said intelligence surveillance and regular patrols were continuing across the vast and remote areas of the Sundarbans to prevent criminal activities and eliminate forest piracy.
Two special operations, titled “Operation Restore Peace in Sundarbans” and “Operation Mangrove Shield”, are underway to dismantle active pirate gangs and ensure the safety of fishermen, boatmen, honey collectors and other forest-dependent communities.
During the operations, the Coast Guard seized 115 locally made and foreign firearms, 10 rounds of live pistol ammunition, 518 rounds of live cartridges, 442 blank cartridges, 52 rounds of .22-calibre ammunition, 366 airgun pellets and five walkie-talkie sets from the bandits.
Members of the Chhoto Sumon, Boro Jahangir, Chhoto Jahangir and Nana Bhai gangs were among those who surrendered.
The Coast Guard said sustained operations and coordinated efforts with other law enforcement agencies had significantly weakened and fragmented the organisational strength of pirate gangs operating in the Sundarbans.
In efforts to protect wildlife and prevent deer poaching, the force also seized around 1,152kg of deer meat, 18 deer heads, four hides, 72 deer legs and a large number of hunting traps during the period. Thirty-seven people were arrested in connection with deer poaching. The seized items were handed over to the Forest Department offices for legal action.

item.title: President warns against self-destruction thru violence, calls for end to arson, terrorism
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Friday warned that the people of the country were destroying themselves through killings, arson attacks, terrorism and forced factory closures, calling for an end to such activities to move Bangladesh forward.
“Incidents of arson and terrorism, killing innocent people, setting buses on fire and forcing the closure of factories are still taking place. We must get out of this situation. No nation can achieve development by destroying itself,” he said.
The President also said the country's fundamental problems remained unresolved even decades after independence, stressing that Bangladesh could not move forward unless these problems were addressed.
He made the remarks while addressing a program as the chief guest marking the 186th founding anniversary and reunion of Dhaka College, one of the country's oldest educational institutions.
Mirza Fakhrul said Dhaka College should be developed into an institution that matches its historic legacy and status. “Whichever government is in power, it should give due importance to Dhaka College. The college must regain its position among the country’s leading institutions in terms of quality education,” he said.
The President described the college as one of the important educational institutions not only in Bangladesh but also across the subcontinent.
Students of the college have played leading roles in administration, politics, education, culture and other fields during British colonial rule, the Pakistan period and independent Bangladesh, he said. “The students of this institution have always demonstrated their merit and competence,” he added.
Expressing concern over the current academic environment and infrastructural limitations of the college, Mirza Fakhrul said there were inadequate accommodation and hostel facilities for students. “There are also insufficient facilities for a good library, laboratories and computer use. The problems of this important educational institution must be resolved quickly,” he said.
Calling for a major overhaul of the country’s education system, the President said many students graduate every year, but adequate employment and job opportunities are not being created for them.
“The education system has to be designed in a way that enables students to use their knowledge and skills effectively for the welfare of the people and the economy,” he said.
Emphasising the need to adapt education to technological changes, Mirza Fakhrul said the world had undergone a major technological revolution.
Alongside the Fourth Industrial Revolution, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way people work and acquire knowledge, he said, adding that the younger generation is increasingly interested in using such technologies.
“Therefore, the use of information technology and artificial intelligence in education must be increased. At the same time, we have to think about how these technologies can be used for human welfare,” the President said.
He said Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman had taken initiatives to make education more development- and employment-oriented and had formed an education commission for this purpose.
Mirza Fakhrul urged the education minister to find out whether the report of that commission was still available.
During Ziaur Rahman’s tenure, initiatives had also been taken to make illiterate people literate through students, he said, adding that 50 marks had been allocated in the SSC examination for students’ participation in the programme.
On the role of teachers, the President said their responsibility went beyond classroom teaching. “Teachers have an important role in shaping students’ thinking, conscience, values and character,” he said.

item.title: Gopalganj slowly returns to normal, but fear keeps streets deserted
item.description:
Life in Gopalganj is gradually returning to normal after several days of violence, arson and crude bomb explosions linked to a lockdown called by the activities-banned Awami League. However, fear continues to keep the streets largely deserted.
No fresh incidents of violence or sabotage have been reported since the lockdown ended on Thursday night. Long-distance bus services resumed on the Dhaka-Khulna highway at 6am on Friday after remaining suspended for around 36 hours. The Dhaka-Barisal highway has also reopened, but train services remain suspended, disrupting local businesses.
Traffic Inspector Jahirul Islam Bhuiyan said buses began operating after felled trees blocking the roads were partially cleared.
Passengers and transport workers said services were running with far fewer passengers than usual because of lingering fears of vandalism and arson. Rickshaw, van and easy-bike drivers also reported poor earnings as the streets remained nearly empty.
Some pharmacies, grocery shops and food outlets reopened on Friday, but most businesses remained shut. Traders said sales were negligible and urged authorities to ensure lasting peace so they could resume normal operations.
The district witnessed several days of unrest linked to programmes by the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations. According to local administration and police sources, Tungipara Police Station came under attack on Tuesday as assailants allegedly tried to free arrested suspects. On Thursday, Muksudpur Police Station was attacked and set on fire, damaging furniture, important documents and several vehicles.
The violence also involved attacks on lawmakers’ homes, a bank and a Border Guard Bangladesh vehicle.
Amid the unrest, Gopalganj Science and Technology University suspended all classes and examinations indefinitely from next Sunday.
To maintain law and order, 27 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh and eight platoons of Ansar have been deployed. Police, Ansar and BGB personnel were seen patrolling key intersections and installations on Friday.
Deputy Commissioner said the situation was now under control following coordinated efforts by the administration and law enforcement agencies. Patrols led by executive magistrates have been strengthened at key points to protect public safety and prevent further violence.
Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain visited the district on Friday and said the overall situation appeared much better. He urged residents to help reopen the burnt police stations, stressing that the facilities served the public.
“If you burn down your own police station, how will the police work?” he asked, calling on peace-loving residents to stand against those creating unrest.
A visit to the town on Friday evening found most shops, tea stalls and usual gathering spots deserted. Residents and traders said fear persisted, with many staying indoors unless necessary. Some businesses also attributed the low turnout to the adverse weather.
Despite signs of improvement, Gopalganj remains far from its usual rhythm as residents wait for normal life to return.

item.title: IGP: Police can’t function if you burn down your own police stations
item.description:
Seeking locals’ cooperation in maintaining law and order in Gopalganj, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir said, “If you burn down your own police stations, how will the police maintain law and order?”
He added, “If you think police are not needed, then you will have to ensure your own security yourselves.” The IGP attended a meeting on the district's law and order situation at the circuit house in Gopalganj town on Friday. He made the remarks while responding to journalists' questions after the meeting.
Ali Hossain said: “I believe you (the people of Gopalganj) will cooperate with the police and other law enforcement agencies to maintain peace and order, and you will keep the area peaceful.”
Assessing the law and order situation in Gopalganj, the IGP said: “The overall situation looks very good as of today. It will remain good in the days ahead.”
Addressing local residents, he said: “All of you peace-loving people should take a stand against those who create unrest. The number of such people is not very large.”
Asked when the 2 burned-down police stations would resume operations, the police chief said: “Who are these police stations for? They are for you, for the public. If you burn down your own police station, how will they (the police) work? If you do not cooperate with the police, they cannot work. And if you want no police, then you will have to maintain your own law and order.”
Asked whether any operation would be conducted to arrest those involved in the recent violence, the IGP said: “The point is, the government will decide whatever the people want.”
Asked about the announcement of programmes by the Awami League, whose activities have been banned, the police chief said: “You have seen before that many continuous programmes were held, and what the consequences were. We should not have to take a strict position against you (the agitators).”
Earlier in the morning, IGP Ali Hossain Fakir, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) Director General Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui, and Special Response Battalion (SRB) Director General Faruk Ahmed arrived in Gopalganj to assess the district's law and order situation following the recent violence.
The IGP then attended a special welfare meeting at Gopalganj Police Lines. From there, the police chief and the BGB and SRB directors general went to the circuit house for a meeting on the law and order situation.
Superintendents of police and assistant superintendents of police from Gopalganj and neighboring districts, including Bagerhat, Narail and Faridpur, as well as officials from the police, BGB and SRB, attended the meeting.
On their way from Dhaka to Gopalganj town in the morning, the police chief and the BGB and SRB directors general also visited the burned-down Muksudpur police station.

item.title: Bus services resume from Khulna region via Padma Bridge
item.description:
Bus services from Khulna to Dhaka via Gopalganj and the Padma Bridge resumed on Friday morning after a 36-hour suspension triggered by clashes, vandalism and arson in Gopalganj.
Buses began departing for Dhaka shortly after 6am on Friday, ending the disruption that began at 2pm on Wednesday.
Services also resumed from Bagerhat, Satkhira, Jessore, Pirojpur and Narail, with buses travelling through Gopalganj.
Idris Sheikh of the Madaripur counter at Sonadanga in Khulna said Ruposhi Paribahan resumed services towards Gopalganj at 6am on Friday.
Officials at the Dhaka-bound Sundarban Paribahan counter said all scheduled buses had departed from Sonadanga without any disruption.
Al Amin of Mehedi Deluxe said one bus left Sonadanga for Bhanga in Faridpur via Gopalganj at 4:30pm on Friday. No buses had operated on Thursday.
Supervisor Kabirul Islam said a bus that left Khulna on Wednesday afternoon had been unable to return.
Services remained suspended throughout Thursday. The bus returned to Khulna from Faridpur via Gopalganj on Friday morning and departed again in the afternoon.
Saiful Islam, manager of the Sonadanga counter on the Khulna-Barisal route, said three buses had travelled to Barisal via Gopalganj between morning and evening, against the usual six trips.
He attributed the reduced number of trips to low passenger demand amid rainfall, adding that services had resumed without any problems. No buses had operated on Wednesday or Thursday due to security concerns.
Roni Kumar of Bonoful Paribahan's Sonadanga counter said 10 trips had been completed between early morning and 4:30pm, with two more buses scheduled to depart.
Ayub Hossain of Golden Line Paribahan said the company had operated only three trips due to low passenger numbers.
Mamunur Rashid of Tungipara Express's Sonadanga counter said its services via Gopalganj resumed early Friday morning. By 5pm, the company had completed 22 trips to Dhaka without any disruption, although passenger numbers remained low. All buses maintained their schedules, he added.
Rasel of the Soudia and Royal Paribahan counters, which operate services from Khulna to Chittagong and Cox's Bazar, said their buses usually depart at 7pm and 8pm.
No services operated on Wednesday or Thursday due to security concerns. The companies were planning to resume operations on Friday, depending on passenger demand.
Meanwhile, an Aiyan Paribahan bus carrying a small number of passengers left the counter for Dhaka at 4:30pm. Services to Chittagong and Cox's Bazar would also depend on passenger numbers, he added.
Counter officials of several other operators, including Emad, Bonoful, Falguni, Shohagh and Hanif, said their bus services had returned to normal from Friday morning.
Shamsur Rahman, a passenger of Dola Paribahan, said he had been stranded in Dhaka since Wednesday night as bus services remained suspended amid clashes and road blockades in Gopalganj.
He returned to Bagerhat after services resumed shortly after 6am on Friday.
He said that after crossing the Padma Bridge and entering Gopalganj through Bhanga, he saw felled trees scattered across the road. Although some had been cleared, the road had not been fully cleared. Vehicles were continuing to move by navigating around the obstacles.
Azim Uddin, a supervisor of Dola Paribahan, said all buses had been operating since morning and there had been no further trouble in Gopalganj.
He said the fallen trees were causing little disruption to traffic, although rain had slowed down bus movement.
Abid Hasan, manager of Bonoful Paribahan's Sonadanga counter, said buses had started departing for Dhaka with fewer passengers because of the morning rain.
He said the company had operated five buses from Khulna throughout the day, compared with its usual 12, as all its services run via Gopalganj and the Padma Bridge.
Clashes, vandalism and arson broke out in Gopalganj on Wednesday over programmes organised by the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations.
During the violence, trees and electricity poles were felled and placed across highways, blocking roads and bringing traffic to a complete standstill.
Transport owners suspended bus services on several routes via Gopalganj citing security concerns. Until Thursday afternoon, activists of the organisations continued to stage demonstrations at various intersections and points along roads and highways despite heavy rain. They were seen carrying locally made weapons, including machetes, hockey sticks, Chinese axes, and traditional oars and poles.

item.title: Young protesters hit the streets across Europe
item.description:
Protesters rallied across Europe Friday against issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.
Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future,” setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks.
The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fueled by grievances that vary from place to place, including conflicts abroad, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities.
But a common theme runs through them -- a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations.
Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets.
“If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent. So let’s go and make our voices heard,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters.
The organizing coalition, which says young people in more than 25 countries will join the protests, urged a “radical transformation of the system we live in.”
Police are deploying in large numbers amid fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred previous protests in France and other countries.
In Berlin, about 1,000 university student and school pupils took part in a demonstration, with many protesting Germany’s rapid rearmament, which has fueled fears of a return to compulsory military service.
“I simply think it’s indefensible to restrict the freedom of young people or of anyone, and to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war,” Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP.
Protesters also railed against rearmament in German financial hub Frankfurt, where some jewellery and luxury fashion retailers had boarded up their windows, fearful of a repeat of rioting and looting that hit the city during demonstrations last month.
While the European Union seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organizers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing.
In Rome tens of thousands took part in a march organized by Italy’s main trade union, which gathered people of all ages, one of around 100 demonstrations taking place nationwide that coincided with a general strike.
High school students also rallied in the Italian capital, marching behind a banner that read: “We will take freedom if no one gives it to us -- against the government, the war and the high cost of living.”
Cardboard models of tanks were burned at demonstrations in both Rome and Milan.
At a youth-led demonstration in London, participants were waving banners that read: “No to war, racism, climate crisis, capitalism.”
While organizers say that hundreds of protests and strikes are expected to take place continent-wide throughout the day, the scale of the mobilization remains difficult to predict.
Among the organizers are also France’s Yellow Vests, a movement that rattled President Emmanuel Macron with street protests in 2018 and 2019.
The calls to protest coincide with the eighth anniversary of that movement, which began as a campaign against rising fuel taxes before evolving into widespread protests over the cost of living.
The protests in European countries have in part been inspired by demonstrations in France.
These began when students demonstrated at high schools in mid-September to demand better learning conditions, fueling a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality.
While the rallies have largely been peaceful, some have degenerated into clashes between riot police and demonstrators.

item.title: White House fires cybersecurity chief after widespread outages
item.description:
Cyber security chief Sean Cairncross was fired from his post, a source close to the White House told AFP on Thursday, following major outages and growing concerns about AI threats.
US President Donald Trump fully supported the firing because Cairncross lacked proper credentials to perform the job, the source said.
His role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies, who has more appropriate credentials and has been Senate-confirmed, the source said.
In recent days and weeks, major outages in America have disrupted travel, communications and e-commerce for countless users, but also affected a top-secret internal communications network at the National Security Administration.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Davies on X, writing: “Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity.”
Prior to serving as National Cyber Director, Cairncross filled various roles as a White House insider during Trump’s first term.
Prior to that, Cairncross worked as the Republican National Committee’s Chief Operating Officer for the 2016 election cycle.

item.title: Saudi coalition issues Hodeida evacuation warning, sparking Houthi threats
item.description:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis warned civilians to evacuate the major port of Hodeida on Friday, prompting threats of widespread reprisals from the Iran-backed group.
The Houthis vowed to hit Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning Saudi airspace was “unsafe” and also threatening Riyadh’s financial district.
The warnings could foreshadow yet another round of strikes, following months of missile and drone attacks and deadly air raids since a truce in Yemen’s civil war collapsed in July.
“The Joint Forces Command of the Coalition is asking civilians to evacuate the port of Hodeida... for their safety,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X.
The Houthis quickly responded by saying “Jeddah and all enemy Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will be targets for our forces” if Hodeida is hit.
They also “warn all airlines that Saudi airspace is unsafe, as it will be the theatre of our operations in the coming hours, except for the holy airspace over Mecca and Medina”, military spokesman Yahya Saree posted on X.
Saree also warned people to avoid Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District -- already struck once this week -- calling it a “military target.”
He added that a power station in Jizan, southern Saudi Arabia, would be targeted “in the coming hours.” Meanwhile the Houthis’ AlMasirah television reported a coalition air raid on a power station in Mocha.
The two sides have exchanged attacks since the four-year truce broke down. On Friday, the Houthis accused the Saudis of striking a civilian boat, killing 19 people.
On Thursday, a Houthi attack damaged Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper in the financial district -- just the latest significant strike on the world’s top oil exporter.
Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces withdrew from areas near the Red Sea’s Bab al-Mandab strait this month, ceding territory to the Houthis who launched a sweeping offensive in September.
The coalition intervened against the Houthis in 2015, after they seized the capital Sanaa and forced out the internationally recognized government. The conflict created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

item.title: Nepal PM to visit India
item.description:
Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on Sunday, his first to a neighboring country since taking office in March, foreign ministry officials said.
The rapper-turned-politician, 36, who came to power following a wave of youth-led anti-corruption protests in September 2025, will meet with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday.
Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan nation of 30 million people, has long had to balance its relations with its two giant neighbors, India and China.
India considers Hindu-majority Nepal a traditional ally, with the two countries sharing a border across the southern plains.
“India is a major and important partner for Nepal,” top Nepali foreign ministry official Amrit Bahadur Rai told reporters, saying the leaders would discuss ways to boost “trade, transit, investment, energy, connectivity, and infrastructure development.”
New Delhi said that the visit “reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal.”
India is Nepal’s largest trading partner, accounting for more than 60% of its imports, worth $8.6 billion, compared with China’s 13%, or $1.8 billion, according to World Bank figures.
Shah, unlike his predecessors, had initially refrained from foreign visits since becoming prime minister.
His first overseas trip was to New York in September, where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly as Nepal was reeling from a deadly tsunami-like flood, triggered by a high-altitude glacial mountain collapse, that killed more than 1,400 people and left 5,000 missing.
Nepal, a largely rural country that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion.
Shah will be accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal.
The visit comes as Shah seeks to reset Nepal’s foreign relations following the political upheaval that brought his government to power.
“This is an important visit after the government formation following the Gen Z protests,” said Kathmandu-based journalist Guna Raj Luitel, editor of The Diplomat magazine.
“The priority has to be to renew ties and strengthen our relationship with India.”

item.title: Pakistan minister to visit India, but no breakthrough expected
item.description:
Pakistan’s Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik will travel to India from November 20 to 22 to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue in New Delhi.
It marks the first India visit by a Pakistani federal minister since the two nuclear-armed archrivals fought a four-day war last year.
The fighting erupted after armed gunmen killed over two dozen tourists, mostly Hindus, in India-administered Kashmir in April 2025. New Delhi accused Islamabad of backing the attack, a charge Pakistan denied.
Since the military confrontation, diplomatic tensions have remained high, leaving little room for official engagement between the two sides.
The SCO Civilizational Dialogue was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO summit in Tianjin in September 2025.
As the forum’s host, India has invited all member states to participate in the event.
The SCO is a political, economic, and security alliance established in 2001. Its current members are Belarus, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.
Ajay Bisaria, a former Indian ambassador to Pakistan, sees significance in the fact that neither side sought to avoid the engagement. “The real takeaway is that the relationship isn’t so broken that India won’t invite Pakistan, or that Pakistan won’t come. That alone is a good sign,” he told DW.
But Bisaria cautions against assuming that the invitation followed a diplomatic breakthrough.
“The trigger was procedural. This forum grew out of Modi’s proposal at the 2025 SCO summit in Tianjin, and as host, New Delhi invited every SCO member. I see no evidence of a back channel or outside mediation, and I wouldn’t read much into that either way,” he said.
The multilateral setting serves both countries, though for different reasons.
Pakistan wants to retain its influence within the organization. It currently holds the chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026–27 and is due to host the next leaders’ summit in Islamabad in August 2027.
Ayesha Siddiqa, a Pakistani expert on military and security affairs at King’s College London, argues that Islamabad’s decision to send a senior minister should be understood primarily in terms of its position in the grouping.
“Pakistan is keen to maintain its position and influence within the SCO and does not want to relinquish its role in the organization. The minister’s visit should therefore be seen primarily in the context of Pakistan fulfilling its commitments under the SCO Charter, rather than as a gesture towards India,” Siddiqa told DW.
T C A Raghavan, another former Indian ambassador to Pakistan, shares a similar sentiment.
“Both India and Pakistan attach importance to the SCO, and Pakistan currently holds its chairmanship. This visit should be seen primarily in the context of the SCO, rather than as a development in India-Pakistan bilateral relations,” Raghavan told DW.
“Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. There will be no real impact on the India-Pakistan bilateral.”
Since the April 2025 attack, India has maintained that terrorism and talks cannot go hand in hand.
“Post the Pahalgam attack, we have a Pakistan policy. That Pakistan policy remains in place. There has been no change,” Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson for India’s Foreign Ministry, said at the end of October.
Pakistan, meanwhile, continues to raise the issues of Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty, which New Delhi placed “in abeyance” following the attack.
Malik, the climate change minister traveling to India, has been a prominent voice in Pakistan’s campaign over water rights. In June, he warned: “We will protect ourselves... if anyone lays a hand over our share of water, we’ll cut off that hand.”
Sanjay Kumar Bhardwaj, professor at the Center for South Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, said the SCO is part of India’s “multi-aligned foreign policy.”
He noted that the forum “doesn’t provide any space to normalize relations with Pakistan.”
The absence of official talks, however, does not mean all bilateral communication has stopped.
Since the May 2025 confrontation, Indian and Pakistani former diplomats, strategic experts, parliamentarians and retired military officers have reportedly taken part in a series of informal or semi-official back-channel meetings.
Such exchanges allow participants to assess the other side’s thinking, keep informal lines of communication open and reduce the risk of miscalculation.
But they do not amount to formal negotiations. New Delhi has said retired officials attending such meetings do so in their personal capacities.
An assessment by the International Institute for Strategic Studies in November said both governments appeared reluctant to resume secret talks, despite the role earlier back-channel contacts had played in stabilizing relations.
Bisaria described the visit by a Pakistani minister to India as “a modest step forward, not a breakthrough.”
What happens next, he said, “depends on Pakistan.”
“If it avoids grandstanding in Delhi and offers credible assurances on terrorism, publicly or quietly, it becomes more likely that Indian leaders will attend next year’s SCO summit in Islamabad. That will be the real test.”

item.title: EWU hosts 12th BELTA international conference
item.description:
East West University (EWU) and the Bangladesh English Language Teachers Association (BELTA) jointly organised the 12th BELTA International Conference on November 20–21, bringing together around 650 scholars, researchers, educators and language practitioners from 13 countries.
Held at the university campus in Aftabnagar, Dhaka, the two-day conference was titled “English Language Education in a Fractured World: Posthumanist Perspectives and Practices”. The British Council and the US Embassy in Dhaka were the partner organisations.
The conference examined the impact of global conflicts, technological changes, artificial intelligence, environmental challenges and widening inequalities on English language education.
The inaugural session took place at the university's Manzur Elahi Auditorium, chaired by EWU Board of Trustees Chairperson Professor Dr Mohammed Farashuddin. University Grants Commission (UGC) Chairman Professor Dr Mamun Ahmed attended as chief guest.
EWU Acting Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr M Ashik Mosaddik, British Council Bangladesh Country Director Stephen Forbes and US Embassy Dhaka Director for Public Engagement Scott Hartmann attended as special guests.
BELTA President and University of Dhaka Professor Ahmed Bashir and EWU Department of English Chairperson Dr Akhter Jahan served as conference conveners.
The event featured three keynote speakers: Dr Jason Anderson of the University of Warwick, UK; Dr Molly McHarg, an English language specialist at the US Department of State; and Dr Obaidul Hamid of the University of Queensland, Australia.
The two-day programme included keynote and plenary sessions, paper presentations, workshops, colloquiums, panel discussions and student poster presentations.

item.title: Johnny Depp eyes Hollywood comeback with new ‘A Christmas Carol’ adaptation
item.description:
Johnny Depp is set to make his return to major Hollywood studio productions with “Ebenezer”, a new adaptation of Charles Dickens's “A Christmas Carol”, as questions emerge over whether the actor can regain his box-office appeal following his highly publicized legal battles with former wife Amber Heard.
The Paramount production features Depp in the role of Ebenezer Scrooge and also stars Ian McKellen, Rupert Grint and Daisy Ridley. The film marks his first major studio project since his departure from the “Fantastic Beasts” franchise in 2020.
The film's promotional campaign has placed considerable emphasis on Depp's return to Hollywood. Its first trailer, released in July, revisited some of his most memorable roles, including Captain Jack Sparrow, Edward Scissorhands and the Mad Hatter, before showing him as Scrooge declaring, “It's good to be back.”
However, the marketing approach has also drawn criticism. Maureen Ryan, author of “Burn It Down: Power, Complacency and a Call for Change in Hollywood”, described making Depp's comeback the center of the promotional campaign as tasteless and off-putting, speaking to the BBC.
Depp's career faced significant uncertainty following his legal disputes with Heard. In 2020, he lost a libel case against British newspaper The Sun, which had described him as a “wife beater”. The court ruled that the publication had established the substantial truth of its reporting. Warner Bros subsequently asked him to leave the “Fantastic Beasts” franchise.
In 2022, Depp sued Heard for defamation in the United States over an opinion article she wrote in The Washington Post. The jury largely found in Depp's favor, awarding him damages, while also finding that one of his claims had been defamatory towards Heard. The televised proceedings brought extensive scrutiny to their relationship.
Despite the controversies, Depp continued working in the film industry, starring in the 2023 French period drama “Jeanne du Barry” and directing “Modi, Three Days on the Wings of Madness”. He also remained the face of Dior's Sauvage fragrance.
Public relations expert Mark Borkowski told the BBC that a Hollywood comeback ultimately depends on audience response and commercial potential. He suggested that Depp's continued fan support could help him regain his position as a box-office attraction.
Film academic Karen McNally also pointed to Depp's appearance in heavy prosthetic makeup as Scrooge, suggesting that audiences might find it easier to separate the fictional character from the actor's public controversies.
Whether “Ebenezer” can translate renewed attention into commercial success remains to be seen. However, its release could mark an important test of Depp's standing in mainstream Hollywood.

item.title: Nicole Kidman adds honorary César to illustrious career
item.description:
Hollywood actress Nicole Kidman will receive the honorary César Award at the 52nd César Awards ceremony, scheduled to take place on February 25, 2027, the French Academy has announced.
The honor recognizes Kidman's remarkable contribution to the film industry over a career spanning more than four decades.
Kidman made her film debut in the 1983 Australian film “Bush Christmas” before gaining international recognition with the 1989 psychological thriller “Dead Calm”, which marked a turning point in her career.
Since then, she has built an extensive filmography, appearing in both commercial blockbusters and critically acclaimed films, including “Days of Thunder”, “Eyes Wide Shut”, “Moulin Rouge!”, “Cold Mountain”, “Australia”, “Rabbit Hole”, “The Killing of a Sacred Deer” and “Bombshell”.
Throughout her career, Kidman has worked with several acclaimed filmmakers, including Stanley Kubrick, Jane Campion, Lars von Trier, Baz Luhrmann and Yorgos Lanthimos.
One of her most celebrated performances came in the 2002 drama “The Hours”, in which she portrayed renowned writer Virginia Woolf. The role earned her the Academy Award for Best Actress.
Beyond cinema, Kidman has also established a strong presence on television, starring in popular series such as “Big Little Lies”, “The Undoing”, “Nine Perfect Strangers” and “The Perfect Couple”.
The honorary César adds another major recognition to the career of the Australian-American actress, who remains one of the most prominent figures in international cinema.

item.title: ‘Emily in Paris’ final season teaser hints at romance, drama and new adventures
item.description:
Netflix has released the first teaser for the sixth and final season of “Emily in Paris”, offering a glimpse of Emily Cooper's latest romantic complications and professional challenges ahead of its December 24 premiere.
Starring Lily Collins as the ambitious marketing executive, the farewell season will take Emily beyond Paris, with glimpses of glamorous yacht parties, sun-soaked coastlines and adventures in Monaco and Greece.
The teaser begins with a nostalgic look back at Emily's journey from Chicago newcomer to an established figure in the Parisian fashion and marketing scene. It revisits memorable moments from her time at Agence Grateau, including her evolving relationship with her demanding boss, Sylvie Grateau, and her many fashion transformations.
Romance, however, remains central to Emily's story. In one of the preview's notable moments, Emily unexpectedly crosses paths with her former love interest Gabriel at an outdoor flower market, hinting that their complicated relationship may not be over.
The teaser also features Emily's best friend Mindy Chen, played by Ashley Park, inviting her to Greece with the line, “Let's party in Greece, baby!”
Created by Darren Star, the final season will bring back several familiar faces, including Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu, Lucas Bravo, Lucien Laviscount, Samuel Arnold and Bruno Gouery. Minnie Driver and Paul Forman are also part of the returning cast.
After five seasons of romantic entanglements, career ambitions and fashion-filled adventures, the final chapter will explore whether Emily can finally find clarity in her personal and professional life.

item.title: ‘Bonolata Sen’ selected for international competition at Kerala Film Festival
item.description:
Bangladeshi feature film “Bonolata Sen”, directed by Masud Hasan Ujjal, has been selected for the International Competition section of the 31st International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK), scheduled to take place from December 11 to 18 in Thiruvananthapuram, India.
The film is the sole entry from Bangladesh among 14 films selected from 10 countries across Asia, Africa and Latin America for the festival's main competition.
The selected films will compete for the festival's top honors, including the Golden Crow Pheasant (Suvarna Chakoram) for Best Film and the Silver Crow Pheasant (Rajata Chakoram) in other categories.
According to the festival authorities, the winning film will receive a cash prize of Rs20 lakh, to be shared equally between its producer and director. The Best Director will receive Rs4 lakh, while the Best Debut Director will be awarded Rs3 lakh. The Audience Prize carries a cash award of Rs2 lakh.
Confirming the selection, Ujjal described “Bonolata Sen” as a personal, poetic and experimental visual exploration rather than a conventional biographical narrative or traditional love story.
He said securing a place among the 14 films in the main competition, alongside works by acclaimed filmmakers and international award winners, was a significant milestone for the film and contemporary Bangladeshi cinema.
Inspired by the poetry and philosophy of celebrated Bengali poet Jibanananda Das, “Bonolata Sen” is a government-grant-funded production. Ujjal produced the film, with filmmaker Abu Shahed Emon serving as co-producer.
Masuma Rahman Nabila plays the titular character, while Khairul Basar portrays Jibanananda Das. The cast also includes Shohel Mondol, Naziba Basher, Priyontee Urbee, Rupanty Akid, Sharif Siraj and Sumaiya Khushi.
The International Film Festival of Kerala is known for its focus on artistic and socially relevant cinema, bringing together filmmakers and films from across the world.

item.title: Arnob marks 20 years of ‘Hok Kolorob’ with Dhaka concert
item.description:
Musician Shayan Chowdhury Arnob will celebrate the 20th anniversary of his acclaimed album “Hok Kolorob” with a special concert in Dhaka on November 27.
The concert, also titled “Hok Kolorob”, will be held at the ballroom of Hotel InterContinental Dhaka. Organized by Twenties Communications and presented by Sense It, the indoor event will bring together music lovers for an evening featuring some of Arnob's best-known songs.
According to the organizers, the singer-songwriter will perform popular tracks, including “Hok Kolorob” and “Tomar Jonno”. Ahmed Hasan Sunny, Masha Islam and Sunidhi Nayak will also join him on stage.
In a statement, Twenties Communications described the event as a musical gathering to welcome the onset of winter. The evening will feature familiar songs, performances by established artistes and special surprises, with audiences encouraged to attend alongside friends and family.
Originally released in 2006, “Hok Kolorob” was Arnob's second solo album and became one of the most recognized works of his musical career. Its title track, based on a poem by poet and lyricist Rajib Ashraf, became particularly popular among listeners.
The song later gained significance beyond the music scene in 2014, when students at Jadavpur University in Kolkata adopted the phrase “Hok Kolorob” as a slogan during their protests.
Ashraf, who wrote the original poem, died on September 1, 2023.
The upcoming concert will revisit the album two decades after its release, celebrating its enduring popularity and its place in Arnob's musical journey.

item.title: PM gifts sports equipment to children on his birthday
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman gifted sports equipment to a group of children and teenagers on his birthday on Friday.
He distributed the sports equipment after offering Jummah prayers at the Bangladesh Navy Central Mosque in Banani, said Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon.
The prime minister also enquired after the well-being of the children.
“Although it is the prime minister's birthday, he gifted sports equipment to the children and teenagers today. He also enquired about them,” Rumon said, adding that the gifts included footballs, basketballs and nets.
During the interaction, Tarique encouraged the children to play together.
The children were delighted to receive the gifts and enthusiastically wished him a happy birthday.
“Uncle, happy birthday,” they said in unison.
In response, the prime minister smiled and thanked them, advising them not to get wet in the rain as they might catch a cold.
He then bid them farewell, saying: “Assalamu Alaikum.”
The children also responded, saying: “Assalamu Alaikum, uncle.”

item.title: Three cyclones devastate Dublar Char, threaten livelihoods of 10,000 workers
item.description:
Persistent rain, rough seas and a lack of sunshine have halted fishing and left tonnes of fish rotting, threatening the livelihoods of thousands at the heart of the Sundarbans' dry-fish industry.
The sea is raging at Dublar Char, a remote island at the southern edge of the Sundarbans where the forest meets the Bay of Bengal.
Huge waves crash against the shore, strong winds sweep across the island, and relentless rain has turned once-busy fish-drying yards into scenes of distress.
The impact of three consecutive cyclones at the beginning of the dry-fish season has left nearly 10,000 fishermen, fish traders and workers at Dublar Char struggling to survive, with their livelihoods hanging in the balance.
The dry-fish season began on October 30, prompting fishermen to head to the island with fishing nets, boats and essential supplies after taking advance loans, locally known as dadan, from fish traders. But their hopes of a profitable season soon turned into hardship as one storm after another disrupted their work.
Adverse weather conditions followed Cyclone Arnab on October 31 and Cyclone Murashu on November 3. The weather deteriorated again on November 16 under the influence of Cyclone Akvan.
The first two cyclones kept fishermen from venturing into the sea until November 5. With a signal No 3 warning in force, fishing activities remained virtually suspended for the first six days of the season. Strong winds blew away tents, tore fishing nets and damaged boats, while rain ruined fish spread across drying yards.
A brief spell of favourable weather between November 5 and 15 allowed fishermen to resume fishing and dry-fish production. However, conditions worsened again on November 16 as Cyclone Akvan brought persistent rain and overcast skies, bringing fish-drying activities to a halt.
Rain and strong winds continued to lash Dublar Char on Friday morning, with large waves crashing against the shoreline. Rainwater entered many tents, soaking rice, lentils, bedding and clothes.
The rough sea has kept fishing trawlers from venturing out for the past three days. With fishing suspended, many fishermen have been left idle, their boats and trawlers anchored in the island's canals.
The biggest blow has been to fish-drying operations, which depend on prolonged exposure to bright sunshine. The sky has remained overcast for four days, while rain has continued for the past three.
What began as intermittent drizzle turned into heavy downpours over the past two days.
As a result, fish spread across drying yards are rotting in the damp conditions instead of drying, leaving a foul smell across the area. Many fishermen have been forced to discard partially dried and spoiled fish. They fear traders will refuse to buy the damaged fish or may even impose penalties if they attempt to sell them.
Kashem Ali, 55, a bahaddar (fish trader who finances fishing operations) from Alorkol, said he had never witnessed such a situation in his 20 years at Dublar Char.
"Three cyclones have hit at the very beginning of the season. Fifteen fishermen are sitting idle together. We spend Tk5,000 every day just to feed them. Where will that money come from if we cannot catch fish? How much more can we borrow from traders?" he said.
Fisherman Rafiqul Islam, 38, said he had borrowed Tk80,000 from a trader to start the season but was now unable to go out to sea.
"My debt keeps increasing while I sit idle. I cannot even send money home to my wife and children. My son calls to ask when I will send money," he said.
Habibur Rahman, 42, a fisherman from Majher Kella, said the situation had turned their expectations upside down.
"We came here to catch fish from the sea, but now the sea itself is coming to swallow us. Without sunshine, there is no way we can recover this season," he said.
For daily-wage workers, the suspension of fishing and drying operations has meant an immediate loss of income. Hiru, who works in fish cutting and drying, said he earns Tk300 a day.
"We cut and dry fish. If there is no work, there is no wage," he said.
Nearly 10,000 fishermen, bahaddars and workers are currently stationed at Dublar Char for the dry-fish season. They operate across five main fishing grounds — Alorkol, Meher Ali's Char, Majher Kella, Office Kella and Narkelbaria.
The areas produce around 30,000 to 35,000 metric tonnes of dried fish annually, meeting domestic demand and supplying export markets, including India, Myanmar and Malaysia.
However, traders said production had already fallen by nearly 70% at the beginning of this season.
"At this time last year, I had 20 maunds of fish drying at my yard. This year, I have managed to get only three maunds. Even those are rotting," a dry-fish trader said.
Khalilur Rahman, forest ranger and officer-in-charge of the Dublar Char Fishermen's Village Patrol Outpost, said the losses would affect not only the fishing community but also government revenue. Fishermen must obtain permits from the Forest Department to operate at Dublar Char.
The government collects around Tk8 crore in revenue from the island each season, he said. He warned that the three consecutive cyclones could cause a significant shortfall in revenue this year. However, he said ensuring fishermen's safety remained the top priority.
"We are repeatedly making announcements over loudspeakers, urging them not to venture into the sea," he said.
With their livelihoods under threat, affected fishermen have called for immediate government assistance, including dry-food supplies and cash support. They have also demanded an extension of repayment deadlines for dadan loans, a waiver of interest, permanent cyclone shelters at Dublar Char and access to safe drinking water.

item.title: Ex-MP Dolon, actor Tamal remanded in Dhanmondi case
item.description:
A Dhaka court has placed former Satkhira-4 lawmaker SM Ataul Haque Dolon on a seven-day remand and former Ministry of Liberation War Affairs secretary Md Mizanur Rahman and actor Md Arif Mahmud Tamal on a four-day remand each in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Dhanmondi Police Station.
Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque passed the order on Friday following a remand petition by the investigation officer.
Public prosecutor Muhammad Shamsuddoha Sumon confirmed the order.
Inspector Md Selim Reza of the Detective Branch’s Dhanmondi zonal team, the investigation officer, produced the three accused before the court and sought 10 days’ remand for each.
Defence lawyers SM Daulat-e-Khuda and Taslima Jahan Poppy opposed the remand plea and sought bail. The prosecution, represented by Sumon and Prosecutor Harun-or-Rashid, argued in favour of remand.
Dolon was arrested from Baridhara DOHS, Mizanur from Dhanmondi and Tamal from Iqbal Field in Azimpur on Thursday night.
According to the case statement, around 200 to 274 activists of the activities-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League, Awami League and Jubo League gathered in front of Rapa Plaza in Dhanmondi on May 22 to hold an anti-government procession.
When they noticed police presence, many tried to flee. Police, with help from local residents, detained several people.
The following day, Sub-Inspector Tanvir Mehedi filed a case under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Dhanmondi Police Station.
In the remand petition, the investigation officer claimed that the three accused were actively involved in the incident and had maintained contact with other suspects who remain at large.
The petition also alleged that they supplied money and weapons for anti-government and anti-state activities, collecting funds and arms from various sources before distributing them to field-level criminals and alleged terrorists.
Investigators said the three needed to be questioned to identify and arrest the absconding accused, trace the sources of funding and recover weapons.
